title: Hematology | Types of Anemias, Mechanisms & Classification
description: Comprehensive medical breakdown of microcytic, normocytic, and macrocytic anemias, including the reticulocyte index, bone marrow response, and peripheral smear morphology.
key_takeaways: Algorithmic approach based on MCV < 80 fL, 80-100 fL, and > 100 fL
Corrected reticulocyte count vs Reticulocyte Production Index (RPI)
High-yield differential diagnosis for each morphologic category

title: Microcytic Anemia | Clinical Medicine & Laboratory Evaluation
description: Detailed pathophysiology and clinical approach to microcytic anemias: Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA), Anemia of Chronic Disease (ACD), Thalassemias, and Sideroblastic Anemia.
key_takeaways: Iron panel interpretation: Serum Iron, Ferritin, TIBC, and Transferrin Saturation
Hepcidin upregulation in ACD vs iron exhaustion in IDA
Peripheral smear morphology: pencil cells, target cells, and basophilic stippling

title: Hematology | Polycythemias & Erythrocytosis Mechanisms
description: In-depth pathophysiology of primary vs secondary polycythemia, autonomous erythropoietin-independent proliferation, and hyperviscosity complications.
key_takeaways: JAK2 V617F gain-of-function mutation in the JH2 autoinhibitory domain
WHO major criteria: Hemoglobin/Hematocrit cutoffs, panmyelosis, and JAK2 mutation
Low serum erythropoietin (EPO) as a major discriminator from secondary erythrocytosis

title: CBC | Complete Approach to Polycythemia & Elevated Hematocrit
description: Clinical algorithm for navigating high RBC count, hematocrit > 49% (men) or > 48% (women), differentiating hemoconcentration/relative polycythemia from absolute erythrocytosis.
key_takeaways: Differentiating relative (dehydration, Gaisböck) from absolute red cell mass increase
Appropriate secondary (hypoxia, high altitude, COPD) vs Inappropriate secondary (RCC, HCC)
Target hematocrit < 45% to prevent fatal thrombotic events

title: Myeloproliferative Neoplasias (MPN) | Polycythemia Vera in Detail
description: Clonal stem cell proliferation, trilineage panmyelosis, aquagenic pruritus, splenomegaly, gouty arthritis, and progression to myelofibrosis or acute leukemia.
key_takeaways: Constitutive activation of JAK-STAT signaling driving autonomous marrow growth
Aquagenic pruritus mechanism related to basophil and mast cell histamine release
Therapeutic phlebotomy protocol, low-dose aspirin, and cytoreductive hydroxyurea

title: Iron Deficiency Anemia - All You Need to Know (Causes, Signs, Lab Diagnosis)
description: Comprehensive journey from negative iron balance to overt microcytic hypochromic anemia, serum ferritin < 30 ng/mL, elevated TIBC, and clinical pearls.
key_takeaways: Sequential depletion: Marrow hemosiderin → Serum ferritin → Transferrin sat → Hemoglobin
Adult male / postmenopausal female IDA is occult GI bleed until proven otherwise
Physical examination findings: koilonychia, angular stomatitis, and pica

title: Macrocytic Anemia | Megaloblastic vs Non-Megaloblastic Pathophysiology
description: Biochemical mechanisms of Vitamin B12 and folate deficiency, nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony, hypersegmented PMNs, and Subacute Combined Degeneration.
key_takeaways: dTMP synthesis arrest leading to S-phase apoptosis and ineffective erythropoiesis
Elevated methylmalonic acid (MMA) is specific to B12 deficiency (normal in folate deficiency)
High LDH and mild indirect jaundice reflecting marrow cell destruction

title: Normocytic Anemia | Hemolytic vs Non-Hemolytic Classifications
description: Complete breakdown of normocytic anemias: reticulocyte index correction, intrinsic vs extrinsic hemolytic causes, aplastic anemia, and acute blood loss.
key_takeaways: Corrected Reticulocyte Count = Retic % × (Patient Hct / Normal Hct 45)
Intrinsic membrane (spherocytosis), enzyme (G6PD), hemoglobin (sickle cell)
Extrinsic immune (AIHA Coombs test), microangiopathic (TTP/HUS/DIC schistocytes)

title: Hemolytic Anemia: Intravascular vs Extravascular Red Cell Destruction
description: Detailed animated comparison of splenic macrophage phagocytosis versus intravascular complement/shear lysis, haptoglobin consumption, and hemoglobinuria.
key_takeaways: Profoundly depleted haptoglobin occurs in both, but hemoglobinuria only in intravascular
Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with risk of pigment gallstones (calcium bilirubinate)
Splenomegaly is the cardinal sign of chronic extravascular hemolysis
